title: Llevar + gerundio: cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo algo

sections.content: Llevar + [time period] + gerund expresses how long something had already been going on -- llevaba gobernando treinta y cuatro años -- a natural fit for describing a regime's duration right before the reading explains why that very durability became a problem. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En 1910, Porfirio Díaz llevaba ya gobernando México, casi sin interrupción, treinta y cuatro años.
items.english: By 1910, Porfirio Díaz had already been governing Mexico, almost without interruption, for thirty-four years.

items.spanish: México llevaba décadas atrayendo inversión extranjera masiva y modernizando sus principales ciudades.
items.english: Mexico had been attracting massive foreign investment and modernizing its main cities for decades.

items.spanish: Este mismo periodo llevaba concentrando la propiedad de la tierra en muy pocas manos a una velocidad extraordinaria.
items.english: This same period had been concentrating land ownership into very few hands at an extraordinary rate.

items.spanish: Esta combinación llevaba funcionando con éxito durante más de tres décadas.
items.english: This combination had been working successfully for more than three decades.

sections.content: Llevar here is conjugated to match the subject doing the action (Díaz llevaba, México llevaba, esta combinación llevaba), while the gerund itself never changes form -- only the time expression and the main verb's gerund shift from sentence to sentence.
